eile 
SEPTEMBER 12, 1966, ST. ADOLPHE de HOWARD, QUE. - - Thirty-three university 
undergraduates Saturday wound up a week-long orientation program at Camp 
Otereke by unanimously endorsing plans to include a tour of overseas duty 


as part of their preparations for careers with the YMCA. 


Most gruelling - - and one of the most rewarding - - portions of the week 
was a three-day series of almost non-stop study and discussion sessions. 
Students, all between 17 and 30 years of age and working towards Arts 
degrees, paused only for meals, an occasional coffee break and, infrequently, 


to sleep. 


Major objectives of this marathon program were to widen and improve lines 
of communications between participants, to promote satisfying and effective 
interpersonal relationships, to develop skills of decision-making and 
problem selving in groups, to impart a greater insight into helping groups 
function effectively, and to provide a thorough and sound orientation for 
sensitivity training. 


Continued 


The students agreed that, in line with the outward looking program of 
Canadian YMCAs, a supervised tour of service as a volunteer in other 


countries would provide a desirable growth experience. 


"The focus would be somewhat different from that of organizations such 
as CUSO or the Peace Corps,"' says R.G. Rogers, assistant general 


secretary of the YMCA of Montreal and one of the program's staff advisors. 


"As much emphasis would be placed on supervision and training as on 


service,'' he explains.
